description.value: The study examined whether anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus, paired with language therapy, altered resting-state functional connectivity and whether connectivity changes were associated with improvements in written naming in people with primary progressive aphasia.

design.value: Participants belonged to a larger double-blinded, within-subject crossover trial, but this analysis used only the first stimulation phase in a between-subject design. Half of the participants were randomly assigned to tDCS and half to sham, with both conditions paired with speech-language therapy. MRI and behavioral data were collected before and immediately after treatment.

task_description.value: Each condition consisted of 15 sessions of daily therapy, in which patients received either tDCS or sham simultaneous with the start of language therapy. The language therapy involved oral and written picture naming/spelling therapy and used a spell-study-spell procedure.

design_type.value: between-subject design for the first phase of a double-blinded within-subject crossover trial

instructions.value: The patient was shown a picture on the computer, asked to orally name the object, and then write it down. If unable to name it, the patient was asked to talk about the picture and provide three properties. If still unable to name the word, the correct word was provided. Errors received corrective feedback and repeated opportunities to correctly say the object name; incorrect spelling was corrected with a model and letter-by-letter rehearsal.

stimuli.value: Pictures of trained words; each patient was given a set of 10–30 words for practice and was evaluated on a matched set of untrained words.

task_performance_measures.value: letter accuracy, defined as percentage of correct letters in trained words

task_description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were collected before, after, and two months post-intervention. Time courses from 19 cortical and deep gray matter ROIs were extracted and correlations among them were calculated.

instrument.value: 3 T Philips Achieva MRI scanner equipped with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were acquired for approximately 9 min before, after, and two months post-intervention using a 2D EPI sequence with SENSE partial-parallel imaging acceleration. The data were co-registered with structural scans into the same anatomical space.

instrument.value: 3 T Philips Achieva MRI scanner equipped with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Structural scans were acquired axially with a scan time of 6 min and 150 slices using a T1-weighted MPRAGE sequence with 3D inversion recovery and magnetization preparation.

pulse_sequence_type.value: T1-weighted MPRAGE sequence with 3D inversion recovery

description.value: Anodal stimulation targeted the left inferior frontal gyrus, centered on the F7 electrode. The cathodal reference electrode was placed on the participant's right cheek. Non-metallic conductive rubber electrodes covered by saline-soaked sponges were used. Stimulation was delivered at 2 mA for a maximum of 20 min in the tDCS condition and 30 s in the sham condition.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: tDCS is electrical brain stimulation rather than MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET acquisition.

description.value: The resting-state fMRI was processed in MRICloud and analyzed in a seed-by-seed manner. The pipeline included coregistration, motion and slice timing correction, physiological nuisance correction using CompCor, and motion and intensity TR outlier rejection using ART. Structural parcels were brought to resting-state dynamics by co-registration, and ROI time courses, correlations, and Fisher z-transformed scores were calculated.

steps.value: The high resolution MPRAGE was segmented into 283 structures using a multi-atlas fusion label algorithm and LDDMM.
Volumes for each ROI were normalized by total intracerebral volume.
Coregistration of functional and structural images.
Motion correction and slice timing correction.
Motion and intensity TR outlier rejection using ART, with thresholds of 2 standard deviations for motion and 4 standard deviations for intensity.
Regression of the movement matrix and physiological nuisance matrix from the remaining TRs using deconvolution regression.
Extraction of time courses from 19 cortical and deep gray matter ROIs.
Calculation of inter-ROI correlations and Fisher z-transformed scores.

model_settings.value: Tests were conducted on the difference between tDCS and sham groups in absolute change in percentage correct from before to after treatment. One-sample t-tests assessed within-group changes.

For each ROI pair, the model used Fisher z-transformed baseline correlation, age, sex, years post-onset, PPA variant, language severity, total severity of dementia using the FTD-CDR score, and left IFG volume before intervention as covariates. Forward model selection using AIC was performed separately for the tDCS and sham groups before combining them to estimate the ATE. Standard sandwich estimates were used for standard errors with adjustment for small sample size; Wald statistics were used for hypothesis testing and P-values were adjusted for family-wise error rate using the Holm procedure.

estimator.value: semi-parametric method assembled with automated covariate selection; standard sandwich estimator; asymptotic two-sided Wald tests

model_settings.value: For each ROI pair with an unadjusted P-value below .05 in the treatment-effect analysis, the before-and-after behavioral difference was regressed against the before-and-after functional-connectivity correlation difference. t-tests were performed on the model coefficients.

estimator.value: ordinary linear regression with t-tests on model coefficients

caption.value: For age, years post onset, severity, total treatment sessions and left IFG volume (in mm 3 ), values shown are Mean (Standard Deviation). P-values are from Welch two sample t-tests for continuous outcomes and Fisher's exact test for categorical outcomes. R-squared (R sq.) is obtained from simple linear regression of the change in letter accuracy against each covariate. Language severity is based on the language subset from the FTD-CDR scale. Total severity refers to the sum of boxes, including language and behavior as added in Knopman et al., 2008. The two groups (tDCS vs. sham) were matched in all measures.
